headline: First profitable quarter, cooling from a seasonal peak
summary_short: UiPath's fiscal Q1 revenue rose 17.3% y/y to $418.4M and ARR grew 12% to $1.90B, with GAAP net income turning positive at $22.5M ($0.04/share) — its first-ever profitable first fiscal quarter — though revenue and net income fell 13.0% and 78.4% sequentially from a seasonally outsized prior quarter.
summary_long: Revenue grew 17.3% y/y to $418.4M on a $35.6M rise in subscription revenue and $21.0M in licenses (20% new, 80% existing customers). ARR reached $1.90B (+12% y/y; net-new ARR $49M; 109% net retention). Gross margin held at 82%. Opex growth (+1.4%) trailed revenue growth, lifting operating income to $28.0M and net income to $22.5M ($0.04/share) — the first profitable first fiscal quarter in company history — though both fell sharply (-65%, -78%) sequentially versus the seasonally outsized prior quarter. Cash and marketable securities fell to $1.42B from $1.69B on $243.8M of buybacks and a $149.4M WorkFusion payment. Company guided Q2 revenue to $395-400M and FY2027 revenue to $1.776-1.781B, with non-GAAP operating income of ~$75M and ~$430M respectively.

drivers.explanation: Company says Q1 results exceeded its own guidance across all key financial metrics, with agentic products moving from pilot to production reinforcing ARR growth.
17% y/y growth attributed to a $35.6M increase in subscription services revenue and a $21.0M increase in licenses revenue; 20% of growth from new customers, 80% from existing customers.
Margin held at 82% as higher subscription-services margin was offset by a rise in professional-services cost of revenue, mainly higher third-party subcontractor costs.
Improved to $28.0M from a $16.4M loss a year ago as opex grew only 1.4% against 17% revenue growth; fell 65% sequentially because the prior quarter is UiPath's seasonally largest.
Tracks the operating-income swing to profitability y/y; sequential decline reflects the same seasonal step-down from the prior (fiscal Q4-equivalent) quarter.

Swung to $22.5M from a $22.6M loss a year ago as the operating-income gain plus $18.5M higher other income (FX gains, lower litigation expense) outweighed a $15.6M higher tax provision following release of valuation allowances.
Mirrors net income's swing to profitability; diluted share count fell to 527.8M from 542.9M a year ago on net buybacks, which also lifted per-share results.
Driven by customer cash collections running about 14% higher than a year ago, partly offset by payments of fiscal 2026 annual bonuses made in the quarter.
Decline from $1.69B to $1.42B driven by $243.8M of stock buybacks and a $149.4M net payment for the WorkFusion acquisition, partly offset by $131.9M of operating cash flow.
12% y/y growth split roughly 30% new customers, 70% existing-customer expansion; net-new ARR of $49M and 109% dollar-based net retention.
